title: Firewalls, Wireless, Embedded Systems and IoT

header.html: 4.1 Understand network security: Firewalls (for example ports, applications); Wireless (for example Wi-Fi, Bluetooth); Embedded systems (for example Industrial Control System (ICS)), Internet of Things (IoT)
the official ISC2 CC exam outline

html:
1Firewalls

A firewall allows or blocks traffic by rules. Good rule sets use default deny: block everything, then allow only what is needed. Rules are read from the top, and the first match wins.

Firewall How it decides Note
Packet filter (stateless) Source and destination address, port, protocol of each packet Fast, simple; no memory of connections
Stateful inspection Tracks the state of each connection Allows replies to allowed requests
Proxy (application firewall) Acts between client and server and understands the application Can filter content
Next-generation firewall (NGFW) Adds application awareness, user identity, intrusion prevention, TLS inspection Decides by application, not only by port
Web application firewall (WAF) Protects web applications Blocks SQL injection and cross-site scripting
Host-based firewall Runs on one computer Protects that host
Exam tip

. Stateless looks at each packet alone; stateful remembers the connection. A WAF protects the web application; a network firewall protects the network edge.

2Ports, applications and rule design

Rule idea Fact
Ports Allow only needed ports (for example 443 for a web server)
Applications Modern firewalls identify the application even on an unusual port
Direction Inbound rules protect servers; outbound (egress) rules stop data leaving and malware calling home
Implicit deny The last rule denies everything not allowed

Intrusion detection system (IDS) detects and alerts; intrusion prevention system (IPS) detects and blocks. Network versions watch traffic; host versions watch one system. AI-assisted firewalls and IDS spot unusual behavior, not only known signatures.

3Wireless: Wi-Fi

Standard Status
WEP Broken; never use
WPA Old (TKIP); avoid
WPA2 AES-CCMP; good if the passphrase is strong
WPA3 Newest; stronger key exchange (SAE), protects against offline guessing
Mode Meaning
Personal One shared passphrase (pre-shared key)
Enterprise Each user logs in through 802.1X and a RADIUS server; better for companies

Wi-Fi attacks: rogue access point (an unauthorized device on the network), evil twin (a fake copy of a real network), deauthentication floods, eavesdropping on open networks. Hiding the network name (SSID) is not real security.

Exam tip

. Use WPA3 or WPA2 with a strong key, and enterprise login for companies. A rogue AP is an unauthorized device; an evil twin pretends to be a trusted one.

4Bluetooth

Bluetooth is a short-range wireless technology for headsets, keyboards and phones.

Attack Meaning
Bluejacking Sending unwanted messages to a nearby device
Bluesnarfing Stealing data from a device without permission

Defenses: turn Bluetooth off when unused, do not accept unknown pairing requests, keep devices updated, avoid discoverable mode.

5Embedded systems, ICS and IoT

Term Meaning
Embedded system A computer built into a device for one purpose (printer, camera, car)
Industrial control system (ICS) Systems that run industrial processes (factories, power); SCADA is one kind
Internet of Things (IoT) Networked everyday devices (sensors, cameras, smart locks)
Weakness Control
Default or weak credentials Change defaults at install
Hard to patch, long life Update firmware, retire unsupported devices
Little built-in security Segment them on their own network; limit access
Unknown inventory Keep an asset list; monitor traffic

In ICS, availability and safety come first, so patching is slow and careful. IoT botnets use weak devices to launch DDoS attacks.

Exam tip

. Isolate IoT and ICS from the corporate network and change default passwords. That is the answer to most IoT questions.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Which firewall remembers the state of each connection and allows replies to allowed requests?

  • AA stateful inspection firewall
  • BA stateless packet filter
  • CA host-based antivirus program
  • DA hardware security module
Show the answer

Answer: A. A stateful firewall tracks connections; a stateless filter treats each packet alone.

S2A company wants to block SQL injection attempts against its public website. Which control fits best?

  • AA stateless packet filter on the router
  • BA VPN gateway for the staff members
  • CA Bluetooth policy for the office
  • DA web application firewall in front of the site
Show the answer

Answer: D. A web application firewall inspects web requests and blocks attacks such as SQL injection.

S3An employee plugs an unauthorized wireless router into an office network port. What is this device called?

  • AAn evil twin that copies a real network
  • BA honeypot that attracts attackers
  • CA rogue access point on the network
  • DA proxy server for web access
Show the answer

Answer: C. An unauthorized access point connected to the network is a rogue access point.

S4An attacker sets up a Wi-Fi network named like the airport network so travelers connect to it. What is this attack?

  • AA rogue access point plugged into the network
  • BA bluesnarfing attack on a phone
  • CA denial-of-service attack on a server
  • DAn evil twin that imitates a trusted network
Show the answer

Answer: D. A fake network that copies the name of a real one is an evil twin.

S5A factory network contains old sensors that cannot be patched. What is the best protective step?

  • AConnect them directly to the corporate network
  • BGive them public internet addresses for support
  • CPlace them on a separate segmented network
  • DDisable logging so they run faster
Show the answer

Answer: C. Unpatchable devices should be isolated by network segmentation.

S6Which Wi-Fi security protocol is the newest and gives the best protection of the choices?

  • AWEP, the original protocol
  • BWPA3 with a stronger key exchange
  • CWPA with TKIP encryption
  • DAn open network without a password
Show the answer

Answer: B. WPA3 is the newest standard and protects better against offline guessing.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What does default deny mean?

Show the answer

Block everything, then allow only what is needed.

R2What does an IPS do that an IDS does not?

Show the answer

It blocks the traffic, not only alerts.

R3Which Wi-Fi standard is broken?

Show the answer

WEP.

R4What is bluesnarfing?

Show the answer

Stealing data from a Bluetooth device without permission.

R5What is the best defense for IoT devices?

Show the answer

Segment them and change default credentials.

R6Which firewall decides by application and user?

Show the answer

A next-generation firewall.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Firewalls packet filter (stateless), stateful, proxy, NGFW, WAF, host-based
Rules default deny; first match wins; egress filtering
IDS / IPS detect and alert / detect and block
Wi-Fi WEP broken; WPA2 good; WPA3 best; enterprise uses 802.1X
Wi-Fi attacks rogue AP (unauthorized), evil twin (fake copy)
Bluetooth bluejacking (messages), bluesnarfing (data theft)
IoT and ICS segment, change defaults, patch carefully, inventory
